narrativeReview.read: Read end to end on 2026-11-22: LEAVE, two TELEOP station-to-L1 cycles in sectors A and B, custody, trough release and support, park, the endgame choice and the empty-start fallback.

objectives.objective: AUTO: leave the starting line with the whole occupied robot (3 points)
objectives.basis: A field-route objective for the empty robot; this package reserves the stowed starting configuration (886.7 mm tall, lip inside the perimeter) and deploys the lip at match start (lip-deploy) but places no starting-line fixture.

objectives.objective: TELEOP: take one station-issued CORAL from the red station
objectives.basis: Cases receive-01-station-chute to receive-16-seat follow the receive-mission trial from the registered station chute to the carry seat; G1 receive trials 108/108; premises station-receive-face, station-feed-speed and receive-captive-time.

objectives.objective: Carry it to the red reef while crossing peer routes
objectives.basis: The drive-away and brake cases of the receive-mission trial (3 m/s2), the 6 m/s2 receive-and-go runs and the sled trials at 1-8 g both ways; weak-pack voltage premise. A frontal hit on the lip is the sprung-stop case service-lip-over-travel. Peer routing itself is a field-rehearsal question.

objectives.objective: Sustain a deliverable load: keep custody when accelerating, braking or contacted, and detect displacement or loss
objectives.basis: Sled trials: powered 72/72, disabled 18/18 retained; the seated-pipe beam, flap-closed switch and lip-deployed switch are selected and placed. Power off: case carry-01-power-off-hit follows the custody-power-off-hit trial; 24/24 required stop and hit cases retained on the squeeze alone. Physical retention and detection are bench gates G3, G5 and G7.

objectives.objective: Release into the intended L1 trough sector A, clear the wall and leave the pipe supported after withdrawal
objectives.basis: Cases eject-01-nip to eject-07-trough follow the eject-nominal trial into the placed trough; G2 ejects 480/480 captured and supported 2 s after a 120 mm withdrawal at every 0-100 mm stand-off, with latch-failed, disabled, lip-removed, short-lip and 125 mm controls.

objectives.objective: Return for a second station CORAL and score it in sector B with the first pipe as an obstacle
objectives.basis: The cycle resets (empty pocket, lip stays deployed). The first pipe at its rest pose is a fixture of every eject case; second-trip.json gives the lateral budget (+/-70 mm, premise lateral-dock-error) and the same-section control. The sector divider is not modelled; G4 measures the dock scatter.

presentation.title: Fixed pocket, held roller nip and exit lip
presentation.architecture: Red 2 B′x · fixed pocket, two-roller nip on a powered-hold planetary drive and deploy-once exit lip on four-module swerve
presentation.focus: CORAL pipe: the receive and eject motions follow two solved trials, from the station chute to the trough. Start with the receive and step through, or play the three recorded trials at the end of the motion list; then read the bench gates under the uncovered cases.
notes: What it is: the Red 2 iteration 002 B'x preliminary blockout, Fixed pocket 1.0, on the carried-forward four-module swerve chassis. It supersedes the first draft: the self-locking worm is replaced by a planetary drive with a powered hold, the receive starts on the registered station chute, the robot leaves when the flap closes, the lip stop is sprung, and four sensors are selected and placed.

Trial-driven: every receive and eject motion is one motion through the solved poses of a free-piece trace, within 10 mm of it; each frame shows the trial time. The lip deploy and the park drive are prescribed. The trials are a planar compliant-contact model: stiffness, friction and restitution are swept, not measured.

Simplified: the chassis, module housings and electronics are oriented-box unions or supplier-bounds boxes; the steer sweeps are 4 mm-stepped revolved envelopes; the rollers are their rigid cores; the gearbox is a planning envelope.

Attachment: every robot part is drawn within the 2 mm check reserve of the member that carries it, with three listed exceptions of under 7 mm whose brackets are not drawn: the electronics stand 4-7 mm above the equipment sheets on standoffs, and the nip gearbox, latch servo and lip switch stand 4.5 mm off the side plates. The posts and side plates land on the two pocket landing shelves.

Not robot parts: the two orange hands are unmounted service allowances, drawn at the end of their reach. The sand-coloured station and reef are FIRST's official field parts standing on the carpet, and the gold pipe in the trough is the first scored pipe. The checker lists every fixture in every case, so the station and the reef appear together although the robot is at one of them at a time; hide the field parts to see the robot alone. The three recorded-trial entries at the end of the motion list show only the fixture each trial used.

Field: the station and reef solids are the official parts as FIRST drew them, placed at the two docks. The check uses the parts the mission touches or passes (barrier, panels, chute plate, guard, side plates and uprights; trough lip, floors, risers and the two branches over the trough); fasteners, ribs and the rest of both assemblies are left out. The trials use the same parts' section, measured on the solids.
Not modelled: pipe yaw and end contact, the chute plate's slots, lip and hood flex, peers. Sizing is by hand formula (structure-checks.json), not finite elements.

Power off: the carry case replays a hit with the main power off. The tread squeeze alone holds the pipe; the limits are in the retention review. Handoff requirement: the nip motor controller's idle mode is brake, so the windings are shorted whenever the robot is disabled with the controller powered. Coast idle mode is not accepted. Brake idle mode is not credited with the breaker off, where the squeeze alone holds.
Bench gates G0-G7 are recorded with pass and fail numbers and are all open; no bench article exists. The guarded-pan baseline A is the fallback if G1, G3 or G7 fails.
Rules: read from the final 2025 manual; the project register is the kickoff V0 packet and the V0 archive could not be re-read on 2026-11-22.

Pocket tray.material: 1/8 in polycarbonate with a UHMW contact face (proposal)
Pocket tray.purpose: Receives the station pipe on a 52.3 deg chute, rolls it down the 15.74 deg floor and holds it between two walls 10 mm clear of its ends.
Pocket tray.rationale: A fixed path replaces the pan's moving receiver; the 15.74 deg floor keeps the seated pipe pressed toward the nip at 0.27 g and the walls square its 301.6 mm length.

Hood (removable).purpose: Caps the pocket 10 mm above the pipe, turns a high bounce from the station drop down into the pocket with its flared lead-in, and carries the check-flap pin and the flap-closed switch.
Hood (removable).rationale: Isolation: without the hood 4/4 receives still seat, and without the flare 4/4 (peak rise with it 7.93 mm), so the planar trials do not show either earning its place. They are kept as the flap carrier and as a bound on a yawed or end-on bounce the trials cannot model; the hood lifts off for the pit unload path.

Check flap.material: 1/16 in polycarbonate, steel pin and torsion spring (proposal)
Check flap.purpose: Lets the arriving pipe in and closes behind it: the pipe is then captive and the robot may leave the station.
Check flap.rationale: Isolation: leaving the station without it loses the pipe rearward (0/2 retained); with it 24/24 receive-and-go runs are retained and seated, and every powered sled case is retained (72/72).

Pocket landing shelf port.purpose: Carries the port floor post and side-plate foot inboard from the port upper stringer.
Pocket landing shelf port.rationale: The stringer has material only outboard of Y 232; the post and the plate stand 60-90 mm inboard of it, so they need a shelf to land on.

Pocket landing shelf starboard.purpose: Carries the starboard floor post and side-plate foot inboard from the starboard upper stringer.

Port nip side plate.purpose: Carries the port bearings of both rollers, the drive, the beam emitter and the lip hinge, and lands the cassette on the port stringer.
Port nip side plate.rationale: The nip is the pocket's front stop and must hold its 12 mm squeeze: up to 457 N per roller on receive and 968 N in the eject squeeze at 160 N/mm (structure-checks.json P1-P3).

Starboard nip side plate.purpose: Carries the starboard bearings, the coupling belt and idler, the beam receiver, the reef range sensor and the lip hinge.
Starboard nip side plate.rationale: Paired with the port plate it makes the nip a removable cassette.

Lower nip roller.material: 2 in compliant wheels (AndyMark am-3462 class) on a 1/2 in steel hex shaft; count and durometer set on the bench
Lower nip roller.purpose: Lower half of the nip: front stop on receive, driven eject roller, and the roller the pipe rolls over onto the lip.
Lower nip roller.rationale: With the upper roller it replaces the evaluation's fence, which no nip could lift the pipe over (finding PD1).

Upper nip roller.material: 2 in compliant wheels (AndyMark am-3462 class) on a 1/2 in steel hex shaft; count and durometer set on the bench
Upper nip roller.purpose: Upper half of the nip: clamps the pipe in the bite and drives it through the throat.
Upper nip roller.rationale: A two-sided squeeze moves the pipe without spin and holds it in the bite under the powered hold.

Nip drive (NEO 550 and MAXPlanetary 36:1.material: REV NEO 550 (REV-21-1651) and REV MAXPlanetary 4:1 x 3:1 x 3:1
Nip drive (NEO 550 and MAXPlanetary 36:1.purpose: Holds the nip against the arriving pipe with a powered position hold, then drives the pipe through the squeeze to eject it.
Nip drive (NEO 550 and MAXPlanetary 36:1.rationale: Replaces the first draft's unselected self-locking worm. Comparison: the worm stalls on treads of 110 N/mm and above (0/4 at 110, 0/4 at 160) while this drive ejects 480/480 over 40-160 N/mm, slowest 0.35 m/s in the nip. The lock is not needed: with the robot disabled the back-drivable nip still seats 4/4 receives and holds 18/18 sled pulses.

Nip coupling belt.material: Timing belt, pulleys and idler (article not selected)
Nip coupling belt.purpose: Counter-rotates the upper roller from the lower shaft.
Nip coupling belt.rationale: Both rollers must turn so the pipe leaves the throat without spin and one drive holds both.

Seated-pipe beam emitter (port).purpose: Sends the break beam along the pocket just under the top of a seated pipe.
Seated-pipe beam emitter (port).rationale: The eject interlock needs the pipe in the bite, and the narrative requires detecting displacement or loss: the beam is blocked for pipe centres X 296-333 mm and clears when the pipe is 10 mm back or gone (gate G5).

Seated-pipe beam receiver (starboard).purpose: Receives the break beam; a blocked beam is the seated signal.
Seated-pipe beam receiver (starboard).rationale: Paired with the emitter through windows in both side plates.

Flap-closed switch.purpose: Reports that the check flap has closed again behind the pipe: the captive signal.
Flap-closed switch.rationale: The robot leaves on this signal instead of waiting for the pipe to settle: captive 0.097-0.195 s after the flap against a seat time of up to 1.351 s.

Lip-deployed switch.purpose: Reports that the lip reached its deployed stop.
Lip-deployed switch.rationale: The eject interlock must not run the nip into a stowed lip (latch-failed control).

Reef range sensor (CANrange).purpose: Measures the distance to the trough face under the lip; the eject runs only at 100 mm stand-off or less.
Reef range sensor (CANrange).rationale: One measurement holds the eject inside the stand-off the trials capture at and puts the bumper at least 255.6 mm inside the reef zone tape for G412.

Lip latch servo.material: REV Smart Robot Servo and steel pin
Lip latch servo.purpose: Holds the upright stowed lip for the starting configuration and releases it once at match start.
Lip latch servo.rationale: R102 needs the lip inside the perimeter at the start; the deploy happens on the field.

Deployable exit lip.material: 1/8 in polycarbonate, hinge pins, deploy torsion spring and sprung stop (proposal)
Deployable exit lip.purpose: Rolls the ejected pipe off a tip 100 mm beyond the frame line at 0.55 m so it drops into the trough.
Deployable exit lip.rationale: Isolation: with the lip removed the 12 V eject is captured only bumper-to-trough (4/4 at 0 mm, 0/4 at 50 mm); a lip pulled inside the bumper face loses 5 of 8 at 100 mm. Deployed to 100 mm, 480/480 ejects over 0-100 mm are captured and supported after withdrawal. A latch failure (lip still up) blocks the exit. Its sprung stop lets a frontal hit fold it behind the bumper face.

Rear inlet upright port.purpose: Carries the inlet walls at the station face from the rear perimeter.
Rear inlet upright port.rationale: The 0.8 m inlet lip is far above any chassis member.

Floor post port.purpose: Supports the pocket floor from the port upper stringer.
Floor post port.rationale: The floor spans 650 mm between the inlet and the nip and needs a mid support.

Rear inlet upright starboard.purpose: Carries the inlet walls at the station face from the rear perimeter.

Floor post starboard.purpose: Supports the pocket floor from the starboard upper stringer.

CORAL pipe.purpose: The finite game piece followed from the station chute through receive, carry, eject, the lip and the trough.
CORAL pipe.rationale: The role scores two station pipes in the L1 trough; every clearance and trial uses its actual diameter and length.

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G0 (tread stiffness and friction): Press a pipe 6 mm into each installed roller on a scale, three places along the roller; pull a pipe along a locked tread and along the UHMW floor
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: 240-720 N at 6 mm per roller (40-120 N/mm); tread mu >= 0.3; floor mu 0.15-0.35. Adjust the wheel count or durometer until inside the band

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G1 (station receive): 30 feeds released from rest on the station mock at dock gaps 0, 10 and 50 mm, nip on powered hold; 10 pushed at about 2 m/s; 10 with the robot disabled
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: 40/40 powered feeds captive (flap switch closed) within 0.50 s of the pipe passing the flap (model 0.097-0.259 s); none through the nip; none back out; 10/10 disabled feeds stay in the pocket

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G2 (eject into trough): Stand-offs 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 mm x loaded bus 9.0, 10.5, 12.0 V x 10 ejects = 150; record tip departure speed and nip current
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: >= 147/150 captured and still supported 2 s after a 120 mm withdrawal; every cell >= 9/10; nip never stalls; departure 0.5-1.6 m/s

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G3 (custody sled and drive-away): 1, 3 and 8 g for 50 ms, forward and rearward, 10 each, nip on hold; repeat 3 g and 8 g disabled; 10 receive-and-go runs leaving 50 ms after the flap switch at 3 m/s2
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: 60/60 powered retained; 40/40 disabled retained; 10/10 receive-and-go seated (beam blocked) within 0.5 s of stopping

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G4 (end to end, two trips): 20 consecutive two-trip cycles: feed, 5 m carry ending in 1.5 m/s2 braking, eject at sector A, return, feed, eject at sector B; record the lateral dock error at each eject
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: >= 19/20 cycles with both pipes credited and no hand recovery; every lateral dock error within +/-70 mm

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G5 (sensing and interlock): 30 seated pipes, 10 displaced 10 mm toward the flap, 10 removed; 10 lip stowed and 10 deployed; range sensor at 0, 50, 100, 150 and 400 mm stand-off from the trough mock, 10 readings each; 8 g pulses on 30 seated pipes
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: Every displaced or missing pipe flagged within 50 ms; every lip state correct; every range reading within +/-15 mm; no eject command accepted at 150 mm or beyond; no false loss through the pulses

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G6 (lip stop and frontal hit): Static: pipe on the tip, measure sag. Drop the pipe 60 mm onto the land 20 times. Push the tip rearward with 300 N, 50 times; then drive the bench cart into a wall at 1 m/s, 5 times
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: Sag <= 3 mm (model 0.99 mm); the lip folds behind the bumper face and returns within 1 mm every time; no crack; deploy within 1.0 s of release (model 0.172 s)

uncoveredCases.condition: Bench gate G7 (custody with the power off): Nip drive unplugged from its controller. (a) Push a seated pipe through the nip with a force gauge, 5 times. (b) Stand the article nose-down (floor vertical, 1 g into the nip) with a pipe seated for 60 s, 5 times. (c) 8 g, 50 ms pulses into the nip, 20 times. Repeat (c) with the controller powered, disabled, in brake idle mode
uncoveredCases.reason: Physical verification, not required to accept the preliminary design. Pass: (a) every push-through force >= 61 N (model 71.8 N at 40 N/mm, 143.5 N at 80); (b) 5/5 stay seated; (c) 20/20 and 20/20 retained, pipe back on the seat (beam blocked) within 0.5 s
